summary.headline: GHCL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR821 crore and EBITDA rose 16% to INR202 crore, with margin at 24.7% after Q1's transient boost.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR821 crore (+11% YoY, +3% QoQ) and EBITDA was INR202 crore (+16% YoY, down from INR233 crore in Q1), with margin moderating to 24.7% from 29% in Q1 on higher energy and raw material costs. PAT was INR127 crore including a INR40 crore net exceptional gain from an ESOS Trust settlement. Vacuum salt commenced commercial production in the quarter and bromine started after quarter-end, while management guided a soft pricing environment for the next few quarters. Net cash surplus stood above INR1,070 crore at half-year end after INR217 crore working capital build.

segments.name: Soda ash
segments.commentary: Management said margins remain around 25% against a 10-year average of 29-30%. Q3 volume will be lower due to annual shutdown, with production loss of roughly 7-10% for the month and about 3-4% for the quarter.

segments.name: Vacuum salt
segments.commentary: Commercial production started in Q2 at about 5% utilisation. Management expects 50-60% in Q3 and about 80% by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Bromine
segments.commentary: Commercial production began after quarter-end. Utilisation is expected at 40-50% in Q3 and 70-75% next quarter, with margin guided at 40%-plus.

guidance_outlook: Management expects realisations to stay soft over the next few quarters, with the pricing cycle continuing over the last 2 years.
Q3 FY27 EBITDA is expected to be lower than Q2 but better than Q3 FY26. The company confirmed this in response to a question.
FY27 EBITDA is expected to be similar to or slightly better than FY26, with incremental EBITDA from vacuum salt and bromine.
A small soda ash price increase of about 1.5-2% QoQ was taken in Q3 FY27.
Vacuum salt is expected to reach intended capacity by end FY27 and bromine by next financial year. Incremental depreciation on the two projects is estimated at INR15-17 crore a year.
Treasury income run-rate is estimated at INR10-12 crore a quarter, versus the INR24 crore booked in Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Vacuum salt and bromine projects together cost about INR168-170 crore, with 40%-plus EBITDA margin and 20%-plus ROCE indicated. Pipeline infrastructure capex is expected to be capitalised by year-end.

Salt works expansion at current location and new salt works at Zara Zumara total about INR450 crore. Salt capacity is being raised from 6 lakh to 8.5 lakh tonnes, and captive coverage is expected to be about 40%, against total requirement of about 20 lakh tonnes.
Board approved INR88 crore for a captive railway siding to secure raw material transport and cut truck dependence.

Greenfield soda ash: Phase 1 is 0.5 million tonnes at about INR4,200 crore, and the full 1.1 million tonne plan is about INR6,800-7,000 crore. Zero-date to production is 3-3.5 years, with stabilisation about 1 year. Land acquisition and some government approvals are still pending.
Zara Zumara salt capacity will take 2-3 years to optimise. Salt field strengthening targets about 3 lakh tonnes of extra salt output over the next 2 years.
demand_pricing: Global soda ash market is oversupplied, led by new Chinese capacity. Many Solvay plants in China are running below cost.

India soda ash demand grew about 1% in H1 FY27 versus about 9% last year, due to geopolitical disruption and delayed solar glass projects. Solar glass capacity is about 15 GW and is expected to reach about 35 GW within 6 months.
India imports were about 4 lakh tonnes in H1 FY27, similar to the prior half. Imports from Iran, Russia and others are tapering, and supply is expected to consolidate to the US, Turkey and China.
Government imposed a one-year minimum import price on clear float glass. Quantitative restrictions on soda ash imports are under DGTR consideration.
Soda ash prices are up about 7-8% versus Feb-Mar 2026 levels, but this has been largely offset by raw material and supply chain costs.

qa_highlights.question: Greenfield timeline from land acquisition to full operation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3-3.5 years from zero date to production, plus about 1 year to stabilise, so 4-4.5 years in total. Land and government approvals are still pending, with some improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Whether bromine and vacuum salt returns will be better than soda ash, and how quickly they ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Bromine margin is expected at 40%-plus, with an overall figure of INR168-170 crore for both projects. Vacuum salt is about 5% utilised in Q2, with ramp-up expected to 80% by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Q3 margin outlook and whether Q3 FY27 EBITDA will beat Q3 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed Q3 will be lower than Q2 due to lower raw material inventory benefit and an annual shutdown, but better than the same quarter last year.

qa_highlights.question: Capital return plans, with buybacks and dividends, given the INR1,100 crore cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there have been 3 buybacks in recent years, and around 79-80% of last year's cash generation was returned to shareholders. Capital will be allocated between growth and shareholders based on greenfield timing and inorganic options.

qa_highlights.question: Why other income fell from INR24 crore in Q1 to INR13 crore in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 included gains from selling bonds. Q2 had a mark-to-market loss. The quarterly treasury run-rate is about INR10-12 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Whether the greenfield capex estimate has been revised for inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not revised the INR4,200 crore Phase 1 estimate, but expects no major change, with Gujarat state incentives partly offsetting inflation. Capex will be back-ended over the last 2 years.

risks_watch: Soda ash pricing stays soft amid global oversupply, with Solvay producers running below cost, and realisations unlikely to recover quickly.
Q3 FY27 margin pressure from the annual shutdown and reduced raw material inventory benefit.
Ramp-up pace of vacuum salt and bromine versus the stated utilisation targets.
Greenfield project delayed by pending land acquisition and government approvals, with capex estimate not revised for inflation.
Outcome of DGTR consideration on import quantitative restrictions, and whether India's solar glass demand arrives on schedule.
summary.management_tone: Confident on cost leadership and long-term margin recovery, but cautious and non-committal on near-term pricing, the greenfield timeline and capital return plans. Management repeatedly said pricing is outside its control.
key_quotes: GHCL is amongst the lowest cost soda ash producer, a position that we have sustained through disciplined operational efficiency and backward integration into key raw materials.

As I have said in the past, the current pricing environment is a continuation of a cycle that has been playing out over the last 2 years, and we expect realization to remain soft over the next few quarters.
We closed the half year with a net cash surplus of more than INR1,070 crores.

adds.what: Vacuum salt plant (commercial production started Q2 FY27, ~5% utilisation)
Bromine plant (commercial production began after Q2 FY27 quarter-end)
Salt capacity raise from 6 lakh to 8.5 lakh tonnes (expansion at current location plus new Zara Zumara salt works, ~INR450 crore total)
Greenfield soda ash Phase 1 of 0.5 million tonnes (full plan 1.1 million tonnes, INR6,800-7,000 crore)

growth.why: FY27 EBITDA guided at same as FY26 or slightly better, with Q3 EBITDA lower than Q2 but above Q3 FY26; growth backed partly by vacuum salt (5% utilisation, 50-60% in Q3, ~80% by Q4) and bromine ramp, while soft soda ash pricing caps upside and no revenue growth figure was guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Margin fell to 24.7% in Q2 from 29% in Q1 and management guides Q3 EBITDA below Q2, but soda ash margin is about 25% vs a 10-year average of 29-30%, and bromine is guided at 40%-plus, so mix from the new lines could lift margins only if soda ash pricing recovers.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Vacuum salt is already commissioned at about 5% utilisation with 50-60% expected in Q3 and about 80% by Q4, bromine began trial runs after quarter-end at 40-50% in Q3, and salt capacity is rising from 6 to 8.5 lakh tonnes (about INR450 crore, under construction).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Vacuum salt utilisation is guided to ramp from about 5% to 50-60% in Q3 and about 80% by Q4, and bromine to 40-50% in Q3 and 70-75% next quarter, which adds volume even though soda ash volume falls 3-4% in Q3 due to the annual shutdown.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Greenfield soda ash Phase 1 (0.5 million tonnes, about INR4,200 crore) and the full 1.1 million tonne plan (about INR6,800-7,000 crore) are planned, with a board-approved INR88 crore railway siding, but land and government approvals are still pending and the timeline is 3-3.5 years to production.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 EBITDA to same as FY26 or slightly better, and said realisations will stay soft for the next few quarters, with soda ash prices up only about 7-8% vs Feb-Mar 2026 but largely offset by costs.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 FY27 EBITDA is guided lower than Q2 (Q2 was INR202 crore) because of the annual shutdown and lower raw material inventory benefit, and India soda ash demand grew only about 1% in H1 FY27 vs about 9% last year, though guidance is still at least Q3 FY26 levels.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Vacuum salt commercial production started in Q2 FY27 and bromine began trial runs after quarter-end, with bromine at 40%-plus margin guided and full capacity by next financial year.

rows.label: Soda ash pricing soft amid Chinese oversupply
rows.why: Management expects realisations to stay soft over the next few quarters, Solvay plants in China are running below cost, and a small 1.5-2% QoQ soda ash price increase in Q3 FY27 is the only recovery taken so far.

rows.label: DGTR decision on soda ash import quantitative restrictions
rows.why: Quantitative restrictions on soda ash imports are under DGTR consideration, and India imports were about 4 lakh tonnes in H1 FY27, similar to the prior half, so a restriction could support domestic pricing.

rows.label: Capital returns to shareholders
rows.why: Around 79-80% of last year's cash generation was returned and net cash surplus is above INR1,070 crore, but management said allocation depends on greenfield timing and inorganic options and gave no firm plan.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost leadership, the vacuum salt and bromine ramp, and FY27 EBITDA at same or slightly better than FY26, but cautious and non-committal on near-term soda ash pricing, the greenfield timeline and capital return plans, saying pricing is outside its control; analysts probed
